messages:
maria: FYI Acme escalated — seeing intermittent 502s from the hosted API through our edge. Started ~11:02 PST, affects embedding calls (large batch). Customer says 20% error rate, mostly 502. Sample trace id: trace-0a1b2c3d.

kevin: Any quick repro or sample request? is this auth/billing or pure proxy failure?

maria: Repro steps from customer attached below. They POST batches of 100 embeddings with concurrency 16 to /v1/embeddings. They include X-Billing-Client header set to their tenant-id. Sample curl:

```bash
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-live-xxx" -H "X-Billing-Client: acme-prod" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"openembed-large","inputs": [... 100 vectors ...]}' \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings
```

maria: From our edge logs: several upstream connections reset and envoy returned 502 with upstream connection failure. Example log line: `envoy http1 502 UC:upstream_conn_failure target=ingress-backend-heap1` and `auth-cache: timeout while waiting redis` in auth lib.

ajay: Sounds like a couple of possibilities: auth-cache (redis) timeouts causing request backpressure at edge -> conn window exhaustion, or upstream pool saturation from large batches. Do we have redis latency / thundering metrics for acme's tenant?

kevin: I pulled auth cache metrics for the tenant cluster: redis p99 spikes to ~450ms during the window, pool waits increase, and edge h2 stream count shows high concurrency. Also see many long-lived streams from that tenant.

linda: Two-pronged short term mitigation: 1) Put tenant on a temporary rate cap (concurrency 8) to stop immediate 502s. 2) Route their embedding requests to a fallback smaller model (openembed-medium) to reduce backend token work. Both changes can be done via tenant routing policies.

maria: Customer asked for repro steps we can run internally. Proposed internal repro: run 16 concurrent curl clients using the sample payload above, chunk payload to 100 vectors each, run for ~2 minutes. Also include an auth rotation sim: flip api key mid-run to emulate transient auth latency.

ajay: For edge config I'd also enable per-tenant h2 connection smoothing and increase auth-cache TTL from 5s -> 20s as a stopgap. That should reduce redis lookups and avoid auth timeouts. We should not make TTL permanent without understanding invalidation.

kevin: I'll prepare an Envoy tweak to reduce max concurrent streams per connection for that tenant (to 10) and set a socket-level retry policy for upstream grpc->http proxies. Planning a small config roll and can target only the tenant routing rule.

deploy-bot: Deploy scheduled: env-edge-config patch for tenant-ratecap + tenant-route-fallback to openembed-medium — rolling 5% -> 25% -> 100% over 12 minutes. Change ID: DPL-5734.

maria: I'll send customer a temporary mitigation plan and ask them to hold bulk runs while we roll. Also requesting SRE to run the internal repro and confirm 502 rate drops after the patch.

ajay: On it — will run repro in staging first and post results. If we still see 502s after ratecap+TTL bump, we'll capture tcpdump + envoy trace for the window.

kevin: After staging validation we'll apply to prod with the rollout above. If anybody sees another 502 burst, ping #eng-oncall immediately.

linda: extra note: consider adding a batching guidance doc for embeddings (recommend max 32 vectors per request for hosted API) — I'll draft a short blurb we can share with Acme. :memo:

maria: Thanks team. will update customer and close the loop once deploy completes and SRE confirms repro results. :thumbsup:
